title: Ezekiel Chapter 31 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 31 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 31 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 31.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 31, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel
The Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon
All the fowls of heaven made their nests
Speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:1 states that the word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel first, before any other events described in the chapter.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 31, to whom did God command Ezekiel to speak?
options: Pharaoh king of Egypt and his multitude
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh king of Egypt and his multitude
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:2 explicitly says, 'Son of man, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his multitude.'

questions.question: In Ezekiel 31, whom is Pharaoh asked to compare himself to?
questions.correctAnswer: The Assyrian
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:2 asks, 'Whom art thou like in thy greatness?' referring to the Assyrian.

questions.question: How is the Assyrian described in Ezekiel 31?
options: A cedar in Lebanon with fair branches
questions.correctAnswer: A cedar in Lebanon with fair branches
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:3 describes the Assyrian as 'a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 31, what supported the Assyrian cedar and made it great?
options: The waters and the deep with rivers running around its plants
questions.correctAnswer: The waters and the deep with rivers running around its plants
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:4 states, 'The waters made him great, the deep set him up on high with her rivers running round about his plants.'

questions.question: What happened to the Assyrian's height because of the multitude of waters?
options: It was exalted above all the trees of the field
It became smaller than other trees
It was hidden among the bushes
questions.correctAnswer: It was exalted above all the trees of the field
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:5 says, 'Therefore his height was exalted above all the trees of the field.'

questions.question: Who made their nests in the boughs of the Assyrian cedar?
questions.correctAnswer: All the fowls of heaven
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:6 states, 'All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs.'

questions.question: Where did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young according to Ezekiel 31?
options: Under the branches of the Assyrian cedar
questions.correctAnswer: Under the branches of the Assyrian cedar
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:6 mentions that 'under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 31, under whose shadow did all great nations dwell?
questions.correctAnswer: The Assyrian cedar
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:6 says, 'under his shadow dwelt all great nations,' referring to the Assyrian cedar.

questions.question: When did the word of the LORD come unto Ezekiel in Ezekiel 31?
options: In the eleventh year, in the third month, in the first day of the month
In the tenth year, in the second month
In the twelfth year, in the first month
In the eleventh year, in the fourth month
questions.correctAnswer: In the eleventh year, in the third month, in the first day of the month
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:1 states the exact time as 'in the eleventh year, in the third month, in the first day of the month.'

questions.question: What was the stature of the Assyrian cedar according to Ezekiel 31?
options: Of a high stature, with his top among the thick boughs
questions.correctAnswer: Of a high stature, with his top among the thick boughs
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:3 describes the Assyrian cedar as 'of an high stature; and his top was among the thick boughs.'

questions.question: True or False: The word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel in the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:1 clearly states this timing for the word of the LORD coming unto Ezekiel.

questions.question: True or False: All the fowls of heaven made their nests in the boughs of the Assyrian cedar.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:6 states, 'All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs.'

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 31 says that the Assyrian cedar was overshadowed by other trees in the field.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:5 states that the Assyrian cedar's height was exalted above all the trees of the field, not overshadowed by them.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 31 describes the Assyrian cedar as having roots that reached into the mountains.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: There is no mention in Ezekiel 31 about the Assyrian cedar's roots reaching into the mountains; the text focuses on waters and rivers surrounding it.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 31 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 31 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What made the Assyrian great according to Ezekiel 31:4?
options: The deep set him up on high
questions.correctAnswer: The deep set him up on high
questions.explanation: This is stated in Ezekiel 31:4, which mentions that 'the deep set him up on high with her rivers running round about his plants'.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 31:10 promise will happen if someone is lifted up in height as described in Ezekiel 31:8?
options: They will be envied by others
questions.correctAnswer: They will face judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:10 shows that being lifted up in height leads to judgment, as the Lord says, 'Because thou hast lifted up thyself in height...'.

questions.question: What was unique about the beauty of the Assyrian compared to other trees according to Ezekiel 31:8?
options: His roots were by great waters
No tree was like him in beauty
questions.correctAnswer: No tree was like him in beauty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:8 states that 'nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty'.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 31:11 indicate about the fate of the Assyrian?
options: He will be delivered into the hand of the mighty one
questions.correctAnswer: He will be delivered into the hand of the mighty one
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:11 says, 'I have therefore delivered him into the hand of the mighty one of the heathen; he shall surely deal with him...'.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 31:7, what contributed to the Assyrian's greatness?
questions.correctAnswer: The length of his branches
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:7 states, 'Thus was he fair in his greatness, in the length of his branches...'.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 31:12 reveal about the condition of the Assyrian's branches?
options: They were cut off and broken
questions.correctAnswer: They were cut off and broken
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:12 indicates, 'strangers, the terrible of the nations, have cut him off... his branches are fallen, and his boughs are broken...'.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 31:9 connect with the theme of envy?
options: All the trees of Eden envied his beauty
He was isolated from the others
He was feared by other nations
questions.correctAnswer: All the trees of Eden envied his beauty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:9 mentions that 'I have made him fair by the multitude of his branches: so that all the trees of Eden... envied him.'

questions.question: What does the lifting up of the Assyrian's heart in Ezekiel 31:10 imply about pride?
questions.correctAnswer: It results in downfall
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:10 implies that pride ('his heart is lifted up in his height') precedes judgment and downfall.

questions.question: What lesson can be drawn from the fate of the Assyrian as described in Ezekiel 31:11?
questions.correctAnswer: The proud will be humbled
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:11 reveals that the Assyrian's pride led to his downfall, serving as a warning that pride results in being humbled.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 31:6, what role did the Assyrian play in his environment?
options: He was a source of food
questions.correctAnswer: He provided shade and shelter
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:6 states that 'under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young, and under his shadow dwelt all great nations.'

questions.question: The statement 'the cedars in the garden of God could not hide him' implies what about the Assyrian's stature?
questions.correctAnswer: He was the tallest
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:8 indicates that his stature was so great that 'the cedars in the garden of God could not hide him'.

questions.question: The Assyrian's downfall serves as a reminder about what principle in life?
options: Hard work always leads to success
questions.correctAnswer: God opposes the proud
questions.explanation: The narrative of the Assyrian's pride and subsequent downfall reinforces the biblical principle that 'God resisteth the proud' (James 4:6).

questions.question: True or False: The Assyrian's beauty was unmatched by any tree in the garden of God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:8 confirms that 'nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty'.

questions.question: True or False: The Assyrian thrived without facing any challenges in Ezekiel 31.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:12 shows that the Assyrian faced challenges as strangers cut him off and left him, illustrating a fall from greatness.

questions.question: True or False: The waters surrounding the Assyrian contributed to his greatness according to Ezekiel 31:4.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:4 states that 'the waters made him great', indicating that the waters were essential to his growth.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 31 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 31.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 31:13, upon whose ruin shall all the fowls of the heaven remain?
options: Upon the ruin of the Assyrian
Upon the ruin of the great cedar
Upon the ruin of the king of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Upon the ruin of the Assyrian
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:13 states, 'Upon his ruin shall all the fowls of the heaven remain,' referring to the Assyrian described earlier in the chapter as the great cedar.

questions.question: What is the purpose given in Ezekiel 31:14 for none of the trees by the waters to exalt themselves for their height?
options: Because they are all delivered unto death
Because they were cursed by God
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are all delivered unto death
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:14 says that the trees drinking water are delivered unto death so none may exalt themselves for their height.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 31:15, what did the Lord God do on the day the great tree went down to the grave?
options: Caused a mourning and restrained the floods
questions.correctAnswer: Caused a mourning and restrained the floods
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:15 describes that God caused mourning, covered the deep, restrained the floods, and stayed the great waters on that day.

questions.question: What effect did the fall of the great tree have on the nations according to Ezekiel 31:16?
options: It caused the nations to ignore it
It united the nations in peace
questions.correctAnswer: It made the nations shake
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:16 states that the nations shook at the sound of his fall when cast down to hell.

questions.question: Who are described in Ezekiel 31:17 as going down into hell with the great tree?
options: Those slain with the sword and his arm
The birds and beasts of the field
questions.correctAnswer: Those slain with the sword and his arm
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:17 explains that they who were slain with the sword and those who were his arm went down into hell with him.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 31:18, to whom is Pharaoh compared in terms of glory and greatness?
questions.correctAnswer: The trees of Eden
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:18 asks 'To whom art thou thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden?' directly comparing Pharaoh to the trees of Eden.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'shachath' (שָׁחַת) in Ezekiel 31:13 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Ruin or destruction
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'shachath' in Ezekiel 31:13 signifies ruin or destruction, consistent with 'upon his ruin shall all the fowls of the heaven remain.'

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Ezekiel 31 to describe the Assyrian king?
questions.correctAnswer: Extended metaphor
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31 employs an extended metaphor comparing the Assyrian king to a great cedar tree to illustrate his greatness and downfall.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of a great tree representing a kingdom's pride and downfall similar to Ezekiel 31:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Daniel 4:10-12
questions.explanation: Daniel 4:10-12 describes King Nebuchadnezzar's vision of a great tree, symbolizing a kingdom's pride and fall, paralleling Ezekiel 31:10's theme.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of pride leading to downfall as illustrated in Ezekiel 31:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 14:11
questions.explanation: Luke 14:11 teaches 'For everyone that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted,' echoing Ezekiel 31:11 where pride leads to being delivered to the heathen.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the statement in Ezekiel 31:15 about the Lord causing Lebanon to mourn?
options: The day when the great tree went down to the grave
The cutting down of the Assyrian cedar
The exile of the heathen nations
The creation of the garden of God
questions.correctAnswer: The day when the great tree went down to the grave
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:15 begins with 'In the day when he went down to the grave' immediately before mentioning Lebanon's mourning.

questions.question: In the context of Ezekiel 31, what does the 'nether parts of the earth' figuratively represent?
options: The realm of the dead or Sheol
questions.correctAnswer: The realm of the dead or Sheol
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:14 and others use 'nether parts of the earth' to symbolize Sheol, the place of the dead beneath the earth.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 31:16 use the sound of the fall of the great tree in its prophetic imagery?
options: As a cause of nations shaking
questions.correctAnswer: As a cause of nations shaking
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:16 says the nations shake at the sound of his fall, emphasizing the impact of the downfall.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 31:18, Pharaoh will be brought down with the trees of Eden unto the nether parts of the earth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:18 explicitly states Pharaoh will be brought down with the trees of Eden unto the nether parts of the earth.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 31:14 states that some trees by the waters will rise above others in height.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:14 states that none of the trees by the waters will exalt themselves for their height; they are all delivered unto death.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 31 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 31 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 31:11 teach about God's justice in relation to human sin?
options: God delivers the wicked into the hands of foreign powers as a just punishment
God ignores human wickedness and allows evil to prosper
God saves all sinners without judgment
God only punishes sin through natural consequences without direct intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God delivers the wicked into the hands of foreign powers as a just punishment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:11 states, 'I have therefore delivered him into the hand of the mighty one of the heathen; he shall surely deal with him: I have driven him out for his wickedness,' showing God's justice in punishing sin through sovereign judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about human pride and its consequences does Ezekiel 31:10 teach?
options: Human pride leads to divine judgment and downfall
Human pride is rewarded with lasting greatness
Pride is a neutral trait without spiritual consequence
God elevates the proud above others
questions.correctAnswer: Human pride leads to divine judgment and downfall
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:10 explains, 'Because thou hast lifted up thyself in height... and his heart is lifted up in his height,' indicating pride precedes judgment and downfall.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the sovereignty of God over nations is taught in Ezekiel 31:16?
options: God causes nations to tremble at the fall of the proud
Nations operate independently of God's will
God only cares for Israel's fate
Nations fall by chance and not by divine decree
questions.correctAnswer: God causes nations to tremble at the fall of the proud
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:16 says, 'I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall,' demonstrating God's sovereign control over the fate of nations.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 31:15 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 15 shows God controlling natural elements and causing mourning at the fall, 'I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him,' highlighting His sovereignty over creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Ezekiel 31:14 regarding God's judgment on pride?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:14 speaks of exile to death and the pit for exalted trees, illustrating God's justice in punishing pride.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 31 thematically connect to the broader biblical narrative of God's judgment on empires?
options: It foreshadows the fall of all proud nations under God's sovereign judgment
It denies God's involvement in the affairs of nations
It teaches that empires are eternal and invincible
It promotes political rebellion against rulers
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the fall of all proud nations under God's sovereign judgment
questions.explanation: The chapter uses the metaphor of a great tree to illustrate the rise and fall of empires, a theme echoed in Daniel and Revelation concerning God's ultimate sovereignty over kingdoms.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Ezekiel 31:18 prepare for regarding the fate of Pharaoh and his multitude?
options: The judgment of the enemies of God's people and their ultimate defeat
The universal salvation of all nations
The restoration of Egypt as the chosen nation
The irrelevance of earthly powers in salvation history
questions.correctAnswer: The judgment of the enemies of God's people and their ultimate defeat
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 31:18 declares Pharaoh and his multitude will lie with the uncircumcised, highlighting their defeat, a motif consistent with Old Testament judgment on oppressors.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 31:4 and Ezekiel 31:6 teach about God's provision and global influence?
options: God's provision leads to widespread influence and blessing over many nations
God's provision is limited to Israel alone
God's blessings cause isolation and pride without consequence
God's provision is unrelated to influence or blessing
questions.correctAnswer: God's provision leads to widespread influence and blessing over many nations
questions.explanation: Verse 4 mentions waters making the tree great, and verse 6 shows all nations dwelling under its shadow, symbolizing God's provision enabling broad influence.

questions.question: What doctrine about the consequence of pride and judgment is taught by synthesizing Ezekiel 31:12 and Ezekiel 31:14?
options: The proud will be cut off and brought low to death and the grave
Pride is harmless and leads to exaltation
Judgment is avoidable through human effort alone
God abandons the proud without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The proud will be cut off and brought low to death and the grave
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes the cut-off branches and fallen boughs, and verse 14 speaks of trees being delivered to death, together teaching the certainty of judgment on pride.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about God's judgment and mercy is taught by Ezekiel 31:15 and Ezekiel 31:17?
options: God's judgment is accompanied by a display of His control over nature and a mourning of loss
God's judgment is always merciless and lacks compassion
God's mercy prevents any real judgment
God's judgment is arbitrary and random
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is accompanied by a display of His control over nature and a mourning of loss
questions.explanation: Verse 15 speaks of God restraining floods and causing mourning, while verse 17 describes going down to hell with the slain, showing judgment involves God's sovereign control and sober mourning.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Ezekiel 31 promotes fatalism by teaching that all prideful nations are doomed without hope. What does Ezekiel 31:10-11 actually teach?
options: God judges prideful nations but does so because of their wickedness, implying moral responsibility
God predestines all nations to fall regardless of their actions
There is no real judgment; it is symbolic only
Prideful nations are always spared due to God's mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God judges prideful nations but does so because of their wickedness, implying moral responsibility
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 state judgment is because 'he hath shot up his top' and 'I have driven him out for his wickedness,' showing that God's judgment responds to moral failure, not fatalism.

questions.question: What doctrine about the visibility of God's judgment is taught by Ezekiel 31:13?
options: Judgment is evident in the desolation left behind, visible to all creatures
Judgment is secret and hidden from all
Judgment has no real effects on creation
Judgment only affects humans and not nature
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment is evident in the desolation left behind, visible to all creatures
questions.explanation: Verse 13 describes birds and beasts remaining upon the ruin, signifying that God's judgment leaves visible desolation in creation.

questions.question: What combined attribute of God is demonstrated in Ezekiel 31:9 and Ezekiel 31:16 concerning His dealings with nations and creation?
options: God's holiness and sovereignty in judging pride and comforting the faithful
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and sovereignty in judging pride and comforting the faithful
questions.explanation: Verse 9 shows envy of the tree’s beauty (pride), and verse 16 shows God causing nations to shake and comforting trees in the nether parts, illustrating holiness in judgment and sovereignty in comfort.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the finality of divine judgment is taught by Ezekiel 31:17?
options: The fallen are consigned to the grave with no hope apart from God’s mercy
Judgment is temporary and reversible without repentance
The grave is not a final destination for the wicked
God releases all from the pit eventually
questions.correctAnswer: The fallen are consigned to the grave with no hope apart from God’s mercy
questions.explanation: Verse 17 speaks of going down to hell with the slain and those under his shadow, indicating the finality of judgment apart from divine mercy.

questions.question: What theological lesson about human dependency on God’s provision is taught by Ezekiel 31:3 and Ezekiel 31:7?
options: True greatness depends on being rooted by great waters, symbolizing dependence on God
Human greatness is independent of divine provision
God’s provision is irrelevant to human success
questions.correctAnswer: True greatness depends on being rooted by great waters, symbolizing dependence on God
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes the Assyrian as a cedar with a high stature, and verse 7 emphasizes the root by great waters, a metaphor for God’s sustaining provision.
